g.text: The widespread use of social media has signiﬁcantly reshaped how individuals connect,
communicate, and interact with the world. While it provides opportunities for effortless
connection, joy, and access to vast amounts of information, it also raises concerns
about its potential to contribute to psychological distress. This map illustrates how the
core beneﬁts of social media - enhanced communication & connection, entertainment,
and information access - can lead to both positive and negative impacts on users.
A user's psychological state plays a critical role in shaping their social media experience,
inﬂuencing feedback loops that either promote well-being or amplify distress. While the
potential for positive and negative impacts might seem balanced, negative effects often
occur more frequently and intensely due to the interplay between dopamine-driven
responses and attention-focused algorithms, rooted in revenue-generating systems that
prioritize maximizing user engagement to drive advertising revenue. This dynamic fosters
addictive behaviours, making it difﬁcult to break free from the negative feedback loop.
A web of interconnected causes and effects
